AT&T, Inc_ location by- jetcityimage via iStock

With a market cap of $144.2 billion, AT&T Inc. (T) is a leading telecommunications company that connects more than 100 million U.S. consumers and nearly 2.5 million businesses. With a history spanning 150 years, the company continues to innovate through its 5G wireless and multi-gig internet services to improve lives and keep people connected.

Shares of the Dallas, Texas-based company have underperformed the broader market over the past 52 weeks. The stock has declined 13.3% over this time frame, while the broader S&P 500 Index ($SPX) has returned 11.1%. In addition, shares of AT&T are down 13.8% on a YTD basis, compared to SPX's 10.7% gain.

Moreover, the telecom giant stock has lagged behind the State Street Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ETF's (XLC) 12.6% decrease over the past 52 weeks.

www.barchart.com

AT&T shares fell 6.5% on Oct. 21 after management warned that average revenue per fiber customer would continue declining in Q4, following a 4% drop in Q3 2026, as discounted bundles, introductory pricing and the addition of lower-priced Lumen customers weighed on spending per user. Investors worried that AT&T's aggressive strategy of bundling wireless and fiber services to attract customers was sacrificing revenue per subscriber, despite approximately 43% of new internet households also signing up for wireless plans.

The outlook overshadowed AT&T's better-than-expected quarterly revenue and profit, its addition of 379,000 wireless subscribers and an increase in its full-year adjusted EPS forecast to approximately $2.40 from the previous $2.25 - $2.35 range.

For the fiscal year ending in December 2026, analysts expect AT&T's adjusted EPS to grow 12.7% year-over-year to $2.39. The company's earnings surprise history is promising. It beat the consensus estimates in each of the last four quarters.

Among the 29 analysts covering the stock, the consensus rating is a "Moderate Buy." That's based on 14 "Strong Buy" ratings, three "Moderate Buys," 11 "Holds," and one "Strong Sell."

www.barchart.com

This configuration has remained unchanged over the past three months.

On Oct. 22, Morgan Stanley analyst Sean Diffley cut AT&T's price target to $25 while maintaining an "Overweight rating.

title: AT&T’s Dividend Payments Fell 46%. Now It’s Spending Billions on Stock Buybacks

AT&T (T) cut its dividend bill nearly in half from 2021 to 2025, while buybacks jumped from $215 million to $6.6 billion.

AT&T's $23 billion EchoStar (SATS) spectrum deal raised leverage to 3.13x EBITDA, blocking any dividend increase before 2029.

Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and AT&T didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat T. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.

AT&T (NYSE:T) pays its dividend holders far less cash than it did five years ago, and it now uses that money for buybacks. The metric that shows the shift is total cash dividend payments. They fell from $15.07 billion in 2021 to $8.18 billion in 2025, a 45.7% drop. Cash spent on share repurchases rose to $6.575 billion in 2025, up from just $215 million in 2024.

Toby Jorrin / Getty Images
Why the Dividend Bill Reveals More Than Earnings

Earnings per share measure AT&T's profitability. The dividend bill shows how management splits that profit between shareholders who want income and shareholders who want a growing stake. The quarterly payout has stayed at $0.2775 per share since the 2022 cut from $0.52. Because the per-share rate is frozen, every share AT&T buys back also brings down its future dividend bill.

Dividends and buybacks together came to about $14.755 billion in 2025, close to the 2021 dividend bill alone. The total payout barely moved. What changed is flexibility: management can raise or lower buybacks from year to year, while a dividend cut damages trust, as income investors learned in 2022.

How Fast AT&T's Buybacks Are Growing

The buyback pace is picking up. AT&T returned $4.8 billion to shareholders in the third quarter of 2026, including $2.8 billion of repurchases. It had bought back over $7 billion of stock by the end of the quarter. Management is aiming for about $10 billion of buybacks in 2026 and $24B+ from 2026 through 2028, out of $45B+ in total shareholder returns.

Free cash flow covers the dividend with plenty to spare. Third-quarter free cash flow was $4.95B, compared with about $2 billion paid in dividends. Full-year guidance is $18B+, so a dividend bill the size of 2025's would use only about 45% of 2026 free cash flow.

title: T-Mobile Raises 2026 Outlook as Service Growth Boosts Free Cash Flow
detail:
T-Mobile Raises 2026 Outlook as Service Growth Boosts Free Cash Flow
Arijit Sarkar
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 11:05 AM CDT 4 min read
TMUS
T
VZ
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

T-Mobile US, Inc. TMUS raised its 2026 profitability and cash-flow outlook after third-quarter earnings and revenues topped expectations. The update points to sustained service-revenue momentum, better customer monetization and stronger cash generation.

The key question is whether those gains can continue while T-Mobile funds network investment, returns capital to shareholders and absorbs higher churn and operating costs.

TMUS Earnings Beat Reflects Stronger Operations

T-Mobile reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $3.22 per share, topping the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.86 by 12.6%. Revenues of $23.58 billion exceeded the consensus mark by 1.2% and increased 7.4% year over year.

Operating income rose 25% to $5.66 billion, while core adjusted EBITDA increased 10.8% to $9.62 billion. The improvement shows that higher revenues translated into stronger profitability despite cost pressure in equipment and services.

T-Mobile US, Inc. Price and Consensus
T-Mobile US, Inc. Price and Consensus

T-Mobile US, Inc. price-consensus-chart | T-Mobile US, Inc. Quote

T-Mobile Service Growth Drives the Upgrade

Service revenues increased 6.2% year over year to $19.38 billion, with postpaid service revenues up 9.3% to $16.27 billion. Postpaid average revenue per account, or ARPA, advanced 4.2% to $155.73, supported by premium-plan adoption, higher fee revenues and rate-plan modernization.

Management now expects full-year postpaid ARPA growth of approximately 3.5%, up from its prior 2.5%-3% range. That higher target strengthens the monetization outlook because more revenue is being generated from customer relationships, not only from subscriber growth.

AT&T Inc. T reported 3.8% year-over-year service revenue growth in the third quarter. Verizon Communications Inc. VZ reported 2.9% growth in mobility and broadband service revenues and also raised its 2026 outlook, underscoring an active competitive backdrop across the U.S. wireless market.

TMUS Raises EBITDA and Cash Flow Guidance

T-Mobile raised the midpoint of its 2026 core adjusted EBITDA outlook, setting a new range of $37.35-$37.45 billion versus $37.1-$37.5 billion previously. Adjusted free cash flow guidance increased to $18.7-$18.8 billion from $18.4-$18.8 billion.

Net cash provided by operating activities is now expected at $28.7-$28.8 billion, up from the prior $28.4-$28.8 billion range. Importantly, planned capital expenditures remain unchanged at approximately $10 billion.

That combination indicates the guidance improvement is tied to stronger service growth and operating efficiency rather than lower planned network spending. It also supports T-Mobile's ability to fund investment while maintaining shareholder distributions.

Is TMUS Worth Buying as Growth Strength Clashes With High Debt Risks?

T-Mobile US, Inc. TMUS is pairing faster service revenue growth and improving profitability with a sizable debt load and persistent competitive pressure. The stock also carries relatively modest valuation measures, including a 13.35 forward price-to-earnings ratio and a 0.75 PEG ratio.

That mix makes the investment case less about whether the business is growing and more about whether growth and cash generation can offset balance-sheet and execution risks.

T-Mobile Growth Remains Broad-Based

Third-quarter 2026 service revenues increased 6.2% year over year to $19.38 billion, while postpaid service revenues rose 9.3% to $16.27 billion. Postpaid average revenue per account increased 4.2% to $155.73, helped by higher fee revenues, premium-plan adoption and broader customer relationships.

Profitability also advanced. Core adjusted EBITDA climbed 10.8% to $9.62 billion, while net income increased 27.3% to $3.46 billion. These gains suggest that T-Mobile is converting service growth into higher earnings even as customer acquisition becomes more competitive.

T-Mobile US, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
T-Mobile US, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

T-Mobile US, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | T-Mobile US, Inc. Quote

TMUS Broadband Expansion Adds Another Growth Leg

T-Mobile remains ahead of the pace needed to reach 15 million 5G broadband customers by 2030. Management also targets 3 million to 4 million fiber customers by that year, while the fiber business has reached roughly 20% penetration after 12 months.

Growth avenues extend beyond broadband. T-Mobile for Business posted double-digit revenue growth, the company continued to gain household share in smaller markets and rural areas, and the T-Life platform reached 32 million monthly active users. These businesses broaden the revenue base beyond traditional wireless service.

T-Mobile Cash Generation Supports Capital Returns

Adjusted free cash flow increased 5.3% year over year to $5.07 billion in the third quarter as cash capital expenditures declined 14% to $2.27 billion. T-Mobile returned about $3.5 billion to shareholders during the quarter through $2.4 billion of share repurchases and $1.1 billion of dividends.

Management also raised its 2026 adjusted free cash flow guidance to $18.7-$18.8 billion from $18.4-$18.8 billion. Core adjusted EBITDA guidance was lifted at the midpoint to $37.35-$37.45 billion. Higher expected cash generation gives the company more capacity to fund network investment, debt obligations and shareholder returns.

title: T-Mobile Falls 18.2% in 3 Months as Risks Cloud a Potential Rebound
detail:
T-Mobile Falls 18.2% in 3 Months as Risks Cloud a Potential Rebound
Arijit Sarkar
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 10:59 AM CDT 3 min read
TMUS
T
VZ
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

T-Mobile US, Inc. TMUS shares have fallen 18.2% in the past three months, compared with a 9.3% decline for the Zacks wireless sub-industry and a 0.1% gain for the S&P 500. The selloff has widened the gap between the stock and its recent operating performance.

The rebound question now rests on whether faster earnings growth, rising service revenues and improving cash generation can outweigh higher churn, competitive spending and balance-sheet obligations.

TMUS Fundamentals Contrast With the Share Decline

Third-quarter 2026 revenues rose 7.4% year over year to $23.58 billion, while earnings increased 33.6% to $3.22 per share. Core adjusted EBITDA advanced 10.8% to $9.62 billion.

Adjusted free cash flow increased 5.3% to $5.07 billion even as cash from operating activities slipped 1.6% to $7.34 billion. That combination shows that the stock decline has occurred alongside better reported profitability and continued cash generation.

T-Mobile Customer Trends Send Mixed Signals

Postpaid service revenues climbed 9.3% to $16.27 billion, while postpaid average revenue per account rose 4.2% to $155.73. Higher fee revenues, premium plan adoption and deeper customer relationships supported monetization.

The volume picture was less favorable. Postpaid net account additions fell to 274,000 from 396,000 a year earlier, while account churn rose to 1.09% from 0.97%. Competition also remains active. AT&T Inc. T reported 379,000 postpaid phone net additions in the third quarter, while Verizon Communications Inc. VZ reported 406,000. Those phone metrics are not directly comparable with T-Mobile's account measure, but they underscore the intensity of customer competition.

TMUS Cost Pressures Could Keep Risks Elevated

Cost of equipment sales increased 12.2% to $5.44 billion, driven by higher manufacturer pricing and a greater mix of premium smartphones. Cost of services rose 4.7% to $3.01 billion on higher wholesale network access, installation-fee amortization and maintenance expenses.

Promotions remain another offset to ARPA growth, while network investment and acquisition integration add spending demands. Operating income still increased 25% to $5.66 billion, but sustained device, service and retention costs could make additional margin expansion harder.

T-Mobile Valuation Adds to the Rebound Debate

TMUS trades at 2.49X trailing 12-month EV/Sales, below its five-year median of 3.17X. Its forward price-to-earnings ratio is 13.35, while its PEG ratio is 0.75.

title: What Could Derail T-Mobile Stock?
detail:
What Could Derail T-Mobile Stock?

Image from Pixabay

T-Mobile US (TMUS) raised parts of its 2026 outlook on October 28, but the stock has lost 31.6% over the past twelve months, while the S&P 500 returned 13.3%. A holder at today's lower price still needs to know what could go wrong next. Much of the damage came in October, when the stock fell 13.3% on October 9 and 7.7% on October 23 on SpaceX's push to become a US mobile carrier. On that October 28 earnings call, management named one risk itself, tied to the phones it sells in the holiday season. So what did management warn about?

T-Mobile Management Flags Rising Phone Subsidies

Management warned that the cost of putting a phone in a customer's hand keeps rising. On the October 28 call, it said subsidies, the discounts carriers give on a new phone, have increased over the past three to five years because the phones themselves cost more.

Management also expects a less predictable fourth quarter of 2026. It pointed to a staggered iPhone launch and higher device prices, and said competition in that quarter will show more variability than usual. Churn, the share of customers who leave, should rise too. Management said the holiday season usually makes the fourth quarter a higher-churn period than the third, and it expects account churn to go up.

That is the threat in plain terms. T-Mobile may have to keep spending more on phone deals to win and hold customers.

What Do T-Mobile's Numbers Show So Far?

Management expects the postpaid business, the segment of customers who pay after each month of service, to lead the growth in about $76.8 billion of service revenue for 2026. That total would be 8% more than in 2025.

Over the past five quarters, T-Mobile recorded its thinnest gross margin during the holiday quarter. The margin was 57.8% in the fourth quarter of 2025, against 64.8% in the third quarter of 2025. On the $24.3 billion of revenue T-Mobile booked in that holiday quarter, each point of gross margin came to about $0.24 billion.

The share price is already well off its peak. On October 29, the stock closed 32.8% below its high of $219.11, set on March 6, 2026. At that close, T-Mobile traded at 14.0 times its earnings over the past twelve months, compared with 22.8 for the S&P 500. The stock carried a P/E of 15.5 at the end of September, and only four of the 40 quarter ends since the end of 2016 had a lower one.

How Worried Should T-Mobile Holders Be?

Holders should treat the threat as real and close, and it has started to show up: postpaid account churn rose to 1.09% in the third quarter from 0.97% a year earlier. The third quarter of 2026 was the 17th in a row in which more customers moved their number to T-Mobile than away from it, management said. The company also raised its forecast for full-year postpaid ARPA growth, the average revenue from each customer account, to about 3.5% from 2.5% to 3%.
